findings.title: No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock causes duplicate loads
findings.body: After the fast-path read returns nil, the code acquires the write lock and unconditionally reloads the assets from disk (or CDN) without re-checking `entryPointAssetsCache`. If several requests arrive before the first successful load (e.g. at startup), they will each take the write lock in turn and each perform a full file read/HTTP fetch, even though the first one already populated the cache. A simple `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after acquiring the write lock would avoid the redundant loads.

findings.title: Write lock held across file and network I/O serializes all callers
findings.body: The write lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer) across `readWebAssetsFromCDN` (an outbound HTTP request) and `readWebAssetsFromFile` (disk I/O). While the load is in progress, every other goroutine calling GetWebAssets — including ones that arrive after the load has started but before the cache write at line 69 — blocks on the write lock instead of doing their own I/O in parallel, and in dev mode every single request now serializes on this mutex. This is a behavior change worth being aware of; it is not a correctness bug, but a slow or hanging CDN call will now stall all callers on the mutex.
